title: AMC 10 Practice: Lattice Points in a Triangle — Exactly 10 Dots
description:
AMC 10 practice problem on counting lattice points inside a right triangle on a dot grid, solved with a rectangle trick and with Pick's theorem. (Level 4 of 5)
A right triangle sits on a dot grid with exactly 10 dots strictly inside. How many ordered pairs of leg lengths work? Vantee shows a neat trick: double the triangle into a rectangle, count its dots, take away the ones on the slanted side and split in half. Then a short case check finds every pair, and Pick's theorem gives the same equation fast. You will also see why 10 and 12 are tempting traps, and get a six-dot version to try yourself.
